title: Cave art
summary: Pigment, engraving, and relief turned rock shelters into humanity's earliest surviving image spaces.

title: Aboriginal Australian art
summary: Living visual systems connect Country, kinship, ceremony, and ancestral knowledge across many nations.

title: Neolithic art
summary: Settled communities made patterned vessels, figures, monuments, and architecture alongside farming.

title: Mesopotamian art
summary: City-states used relief, sculpture, seals, and architecture to picture ritual and power.

title: Ancient Egyptian art
summary: A durable visual grammar joined divine order, royal authority, daily life, and the afterlife.

title: Indus Valley art
summary: Small seals, terracotta figures, metalwork, and planned cities reveal an urban visual culture.

title: Ancient Greek art
summary: Artists repeatedly reworked the human figure through pottery, sculpture, painting, and temples.

title: Roman art
summary: Portraiture, illusionistic rooms, monuments, and mosaics carried imperial and domestic stories.

title: Achaemenid Persian art
summary: Palatial reliefs and architecture joined regional forms into a precise language of empire.

title: Gandharan art
summary: Buddhist subjects met Hellenistic and South Asian forms along long-distance trade routes.

title: Hindu temple art
summary: Temple architecture and sculpture made sacred narratives spatial, rhythmic, and bodily.

title: Han dynasty art
summary: Tombs, lacquer, textiles, bronzes, and reliefs mapped an expanding imperial world.

title: Olmec art
summary: Monumental stone heads and small ritual objects established enduring Mesoamerican forms.

title: Maya art
summary: Architecture, painted vessels, books, and carved monuments bound image, text, and time.

title: Moche art
summary: Ceramics, metalwork, and murals pictured ceremony, ecology, conflict, and social roles.

title: Nok terracottas
summary: Distinctive hollow terracotta figures preserve one of West Africa's earliest sculptural traditions.

title: Byzantine art
summary: Mosaics, icons, manuscripts, and churches shaped sacred presence through light and gold.

title: Islamic art
summary: Calligraphy, geometry, vegetal pattern, objects, and architecture developed across connected regions.

title: Gothic art
summary: Soaring structures, stained glass, sculpture, and manuscripts organized narrative through light.

title: Song dynasty painting
summary: Monumental landscapes and intimate studies made observation a philosophical practice.

title: Yamato-e
summary: Japanese court painting unfolded seasons, places, and literature across screens and handscrolls.

title: Goryeo celadon
summary: Korean potters refined translucent glazes and inlay into quiet, technically exact surfaces.

title: Khmer art
summary: Temple complexes and sculpture joined Hindu and Buddhist cosmologies to royal landscapes.

title: Ethiopian Christian art
summary: Churches, icons, crosses, and manuscripts sustained a distinct Christian visual tradition.

title: Ife art
summary: Naturalistic copper-alloy and terracotta heads articulated Yoruba sacred and royal identity.

title: Andean textiles
summary: Fiber, dye, and structure carried status, cosmology, and information across Andean societies.

title: Persian miniature
summary: Dense color, flattened space, and fine detail animated poetry, history, and court life.

title: Mughal painting
summary: Court workshops fused Persian, South Asian, and European observation in precise miniatures.

title: Renaissance
summary: Perspective, anatomy, antiquity, and patronage reshaped painting, sculpture, and architecture.

title: Mannerism
summary: Elongated figures, unstable space, and cultivated artifice stretched Renaissance balance.

title: Baroque
summary: Dramatic light, movement, scale, and illusion made persuasion physically immediate.

title: Dutch Golden Age
summary: A broad art market supported portraiture, landscape, still life, and domestic observation.

title: Ukiyo-e
summary: Woodblock prints circulated actors, landscapes, fashion, and urban pleasures at scale.

title: Benin court art
summary: Royal workshops cast and carved histories of the Edo court with extraordinary control.

title: Oceanic art
summary: Navigation, genealogy, exchange, and ceremony informed objects across many Pacific cultures.

title: Neoclassicism
summary: Artists used classical form to stage civic virtue, empire, revolution, and restraint.

title: Romanticism
summary: Emotion, imagination, nature, history, and political upheaval displaced classical certainty.

title: Realism
summary: Contemporary labor and ordinary life became subjects for unsentimental, materially direct art.

title: Impressionism
summary: Broken color and visible brushwork registered changing light and modern experience.

title: Post-Impressionism
summary: Artists pushed beyond optical immediacy toward structure, symbol, emotion, and personal systems.

title: Symbolism
summary: Dream, myth, spirituality, and suggestion challenged naturalism's visible world.

title: Arts and Crafts
summary: Designers tied skilled making and useful beauty to criticism of industrial production.

title: Art Nouveau
summary: Sinuous organic line linked posters, interiors, objects, architecture, and total design.

title: Fauvism
summary: Independent, high-key color became a structural force rather than a descriptive one.

title: Expressionism
summary: Distorted form and urgent color externalized psychic, social, and spiritual pressure.

title: Cubism
summary: Fragmented viewpoints rebuilt objects and space as interlocking signs and planes.

title: Futurism
summary: Speed, machines, noise, and violent change became subjects and formal methods.

title: Dada
summary: Chance, absurdity, collage, and readymades attacked art's institutions and wartime reason.

title: Surrealism
summary: Dream, automatism, and unlikely encounters opened images to unconscious association.

title: Constructivism
summary: Geometric abstraction was directed toward material, communication, and collective social use.

title: Bauhaus
summary: A school joined art, craft, typography, architecture, and industrial production.

title: Harlem Renaissance
summary: Black artists shaped modern identity through painting, photography, print, music, and literature.

title: Mexican muralism
summary: Public murals connected revolutionary history, labor, Indigenous heritage, and mass audiences.

title: Abstract Expressionism
summary: Scale, gesture, stain, and fields of color made painting an event and environment.

title: Pop Art
summary: Advertising, comics, products, and celebrity imagery collapsed distinctions between art and commerce.

title: Minimalism
summary: Serial form, industrial materials, and literal space reduced composition to direct encounter.

title: Conceptual art
summary: Instructions, language, documentation, and systems made the idea the primary medium.

title: Land art
summary: Artists worked directly with sites, earth, duration, and ecological scale.

title: Feminist art
summary: Artists challenged exclusion, representation, authorship, labor, and the politics of the body.

title: Street art
summary: Unsanctioned marks, murals, stencils, and interventions turned public space into a medium.

title: Digital art
summary: Code, networks, computation, and electronic images changed how work is made and distributed.

title: Gutai
summary: Japanese artists made matter, action, destruction, and outdoor display active collaborators.

title: Bengal School
summary: Artists developed anti-colonial modernisms through Mughal, Japanese, and Indic sources.

title: Papunya Tula
summary: Western Desert artists translated community-held visual knowledge into a new painting movement.
